_doc: Implied equity risk premium for the US market. Damodaran's signature metric — derived from current S&P 500 price and dividend+buyback yield, NOT historical realised returns. Updated monthly.
_source: Damodaran 'Implied ERP for the S&P 500', headline figure published on his home page
_methodology: Damodaran calc: implied ERP = (expected cash flows / current price) - risk_free_rate. Cash flows = current div + buybacks, growing at expected real rate (capped at risk-free).
_variant_used: Trailing 12 month, with adjusted payout — Damodaran's headline measure and the one he uses in his own valuations. The alternatives below are published alongside it and are NOT interchangeable; swapping variants moves cost of equity by up to 257bps.

components._doc: Decomposition for transparency — not used directly in calc but useful for narrative

_pairing_caveat: Damodaran computed this 4.28% against a US treasury rate of 4.74% on 2026-08-01. risk_free_rate.json holds 4.63% (FRED DGS10, 2026-08-13) — a different date and an 11bps difference. Cost of equity in this codebase is therefore rf(4.63) + beta x ERP(4.28), which is internally consistent but not byte-identical to Damodaran's own pairing. The 11bps is immaterial next to beta and margin uncertainty; recorded so nobody rediscovers it as a discrepancy.

_previous_snapshot._note: Superseded 2026-08-16. ERP compressed 32bps while the risk-free rose 28bps — the two largely offset, so cost of equity is roughly unchanged.
